doc: Places a card can sit that no state in internal/pipelinefsm/pipeline-fsm.json describes. Found by driving the real DeriveBoardCard over the real marker vocabulary and comparing what comes out against what the machine claims. Recorded rather than fixed: what to do about each is a separate question, and answering it here — by widening the document until nothing is left over — is the move that would make the machine agree with anything.
bound: A LOWER BOUND. An entry here is real; an absence proves nothing. What no longer bounds it is thread DEPTH: this said a placement reachable only from three markers could not appear, and that was an assumption. Measured 2026-08-09 — the placement set saturates at two. All 36^3 ordered triples yield the same 27 placements pairs do, and a one-off probe of all 36^4 quadruples added none either; triples are now enumerated by the shipped check so a change that makes a third marker matter fails it. What still bounds it is marker SHAPE: every header is seeded with one body and the options block with one stage-and-count, so a placement that needs a particular body cannot appear.

planning/queued.note: See implementation/queued — one cause, three stages (optionStages is planning, implementation, verification; the done stage raises its decisions against implementation, so there is no done/queued).

implementation/queued.note: A decision is recorded and the stage it named is requeued, but no agent has posted that stage's started marker. BoardQueued exists to stop the stuck-running pass redding a just-decided card (SC-1320) — and it does that by being a state that pass does not look at. Nor does any other: every reconcile pass keys on running, outage, a handoff, a loop, or a container. optionChosenQueued's own doc says a deferred launch can leave a card here indefinitely.
implementation/queued.known: That a card CAN sit here indefinitely is documented in the code. Whether one ever HAS is now partly measured: of the 59 histories in internal/pipelinefsm/testdata/replay-corpus.json, 12 record a decision — 13 in all, SC-2596 twice — and every one is followed by a later marker. Six were followed by the relaunch's started marker, four by the claim that precedes it, and three by [human:needs-planning]: the plan gate refusing the relaunch, which is an exit the machine already describes (launch-refused-no-plan). None was left queued.
implementation/queued.not_known: The corpus is a snapshot of the 80 most-recently-updated tickets, so this says no card was queued THEN, not that none is now, and it says nothing about older work. Reaching the hole needs a launch-critical doctor check to fail at the moment a decision is answered, with no second daemon to take the work — rare by construction, which is what 13 clean decisions are consistent with, and is not evidence that it cannot happen.

hidden/.reached_by: a ticket whose tracker status is done or closed
hidden/.note: Closing a ticket takes it off the board from ANY state, and reaper.md treats close as cancellation — it stops the ticket's agents. So it is a transition out of every state at once, fired from outside the marker bus, recorded in no comment. That is why fifty-nine replayed histories never surfaced it and a state-space enumeration does: the two measurements are blind to different things.
hidden/.measured: 2026-08-08, every closed ticket on the PM tracker (382, no sampling). Each was replayed through DeriveBoardCard as if still open, to find where the card was when the close took it off the board. 125 carried no markers at all — never in the pipeline. 197 were closed AT REST, on a terminal the machine already declares: 173 merged, 13 resolved-no-fix, 11 nothing-to-do. The remaining 60 were closed OUT OF a non-terminal state, which is the transition the document does not have.
hidden/.shape_of_those_60: 35 from `stopped` (30 done/failed, 3 implementation/failed, 2 planning/failed) — a person giving up on a card the machine had already given up on. 16 from a state that was WAITING for a gesture rather than working (7 reviewed, 5 handed-off, 4 planned). 5 from backlog. Only 4 from a RUNNING state, where closing kills a live agent: SC-110, SC-296, SC-1865, SC-2400.
hidden/.era: Rates over tickets that entered the pipeline, by ticket-number band: SC-<1000 29/99, SC-1000s 13/66, SC-2000s 14/55, SC-3000s 4/37. Declining but present throughout, so this is NOT retired behaviour — the `legacy` question was asked and answered against the numbers rather than assumed. In the current band all four are `stopped` after a failed deploy, and none is a close from a running state.
hidden/.not_known: Why each was closed. The tracker records that a person closed it, not whether the work was abandoned, shipped another way, or folded into another ticket — and SC-1290's and SC-1692's threads suggest at least the first two both happen. Nothing here says the missing edge should be added; it says how often something walks through the gap where one would be.

ideas/.reached_by: a ticket carrying the idea label
ideas/.note: The machine's initial state is `filed`, and idea-to-PM promotion is a label swap rather than a marker, so an idea is arguably before the machine rather than missing from it. Recorded because the enumeration cannot tell 'deliberately outside' from 'left out' — only a person can.
ideas/.known: Read in code 2026-08-09, three facts. (1) Promotion posts NO marker: RunIdeaPromote (cmd/cmdauto/semantic.go) is one EditIssue with RemoveLabels and nothing else, so ideas -> filed is invisible to the marker bus in exactly the way close is — which is why replaying markers can never see this edge, and why it took a state-space enumeration to surface it. (2) Membership is the label and only the label: DeriveBoardCard returns the Ideas stage before it looks at a single comment, deliberately (board_state.go), so an idea-labelled ticket that somehow carries pipeline markers renders as an idea and its real pipeline position is hidden. (3) The word `idea` appears NOWHERE in pipeline-fsm.json, while `filed` claims board (backlog, "") unconditionally — so for an idea-labelled ticket that state's `holds` is satisfied and its `board` is wrong.
ideas/.not_known: How often (2) actually happens — whether any idea-labelled ticket carries pipeline markers, which is the number that would say if the hiding is theoretical or real. It needs the label on every ticket, which the local replay corpus does not record (it stores key and markers only) and the tracker was vault-locked when this was written. This is the one of the three still unmeasured against real tickets.
